accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 3-LS4-4 (some organisms survive and reproduce, some move, some move in, some die), the National Curriculum in England Year 4 living things and their habitats statement, and named field sources: American pika loss at low, hot sites and upslope shifts in the Great Basin (Beever et al. 2011); treeline advance with warming (Harsch et al. 2009); fireweed (Chamaenerion angustifolium) as a wind-dispersed post-fire coloniser and black-backed woodpeckers moving into burnt forest to feed on wood-boring beetle larvae (USDA Forest Service Fire Effects Information System); soil insulating organisms a few centimetres down during fires. The 150 m per 1 °C figure follows the standard environmental lapse rate of about 6.5 °C per km. The drought food-chain bars and mountain zones are labelled as simple models, not data.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented misconceptions (Bishop and Anderson 1990; AAAS Project 2061 benchmarks on natural selection): organisms change their bodies because they need to (fish growing legs, pikas 'changing to like heat'), every change harms every organism, plants can move away or choose to stay, and a change only affects animals that eat the lost resource directly. The predictions and challenge feedback address each one.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab, including flag_envimp.js (human impact causes), flag_vary.js (variation and survival) and flag_habnd.js (habitat needs). Only this lab sorts organisms into survive / move away / move in / die outcomes for two different changes, warms a zoned mountain so the pika's cold band shrinks to nothing, orders post-fire succession stages, and steps a drought year by year along a grass–rabbit–fox chain.

lab_teaches.evidence: Five steps and a challenge: the drying pond introduces three outcomes from whether an organism can move and what it needs; the mountain shows a slow change and a range shift that runs out of room; the fire produces all four outcomes in one event; regrowth ordering shows a changed place keeps changing; the food-chain model shows knock-on effects arriving a year later at each link. Wrong sorts are refused with the organism's specific reason.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: what happens to pond fish ('They walk to another pond'), where cold-loving life goes as a mountain warms ('down in the warm valley', 'stay put'), whether fire brings newcomers ('No: a fire only kills'), plus the foxes-after-drought prediction ('Nothing: foxes eat rabbits, not grass') — four in all, each disproved by the step that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eight wrong-answer messages: assuming all organisms can move, adapting on demand, mismatching needs, change only harms, plants choosing, no knock-on along a food chain, moving downhill to cool, and expecting trees to return first. Each names the slip and states the correct idea.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid text grade 2.4 and adult 8.8 (limits 6.5 and 9.5). Kid paragraphs use a pond, a mountain and a food chain with short sentences; 'pika' is explained as a small furry animal that needs cold. Card labels are one to three words so they fit two per row at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content passed: no filler patterns and explanation overlap under 12% with 674 (human impact), 885 (variation), 733 (habitats and needs) and the rainforest lessons. Each kid paragraph does one job: what dies and what leaves, what moves in, a slow change, and knock-on effects plus why bodies cannot change on demand.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 × 640 (2x) in light and dark for every step before and after Show me. Fixes made from the first sheets: the 'alpine flowers' label ran off the right edge and now sits centred in its band; bin summaries showed 'soil, soil' and now use clear card names (Deep-soil earthworms, Buried seeds); bins are now placed above the measured feedback box; canvas height raised to 1.3 × width so cards and bins never touch.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a button twin (pick any card and send it to any box; Warm 1 °C; each regrowth stage; Next year and Bring rain). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with each card's state, the warming level, the stage order or the three population values. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations and no console errors.
